newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank cuts overnight rates.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank cuts overnight rates.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Thursday it cut its overnight rates by two percentage points each.
The overnight borrowing rate is now 14 percent, while the lending rate is 16 percent.
This is the third cut in as many weeks.

The Bank raised its overnight rates to a two-hear high in mid-May to defend the peso as the local stock market was pounded by fears the Philippines was about to suffer the same financial troubles as Thailand.
"We have to be prudent about it," Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza told Reuters of the Bank's strategy to gradually cut rates as the peso becomes more stable.
He said the Central Bank is likely to lower rates further in the future since "evidence points to a cut in rates," but gave no time-frame.
The Central Bank will also adjust downwards its term reverse repo rates, he added.
